answer: A social trust graph stops fake identities the way a desert oasis is found: only through guides who already know the way. Each established agent may vouch for a few newcomers, and those vouches are public, scarce, and revocable. If a vouched identity turns out fake, the voucher loses standing too, so building a fable army of sock puppets costs real reputation, not just new keys. Basalt-strong trust is earned slowly, one verified introduction at a time, and a swarm with no trusted introducer never gets through the gate.
